title: Caro-Kann Defense: Panov Attack
line: White plays for active pieces with a lone pawn in the center; Black sits a knight in front of it.

steps.text: In the Panov, White traded pawns and then hit your center pawn with another.
Bring the knight out to guard your pawn.
Push the pawn on e7 one square. It guards d5 again and frees your bishop.

also.b8c6: That also works. This lesson goes on with the pawn.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out, so you can castle.

also.f8b4: That also works. This lesson puts the bishop on e7.

steps.text: Take back with the knight. It sits on d5, right in front of White's pawn.

also.e6d5: That works too, and the pawns match again. This lesson takes with the knight.

steps.text: Tap the white pawn that has no white pawns on the files beside it.
steps.after: A lone pawn like this is hard to guard. Black keeps a piece on the square in front of it.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out. It hits the lone pawn.
Castle. Your king goes to safety, and a rook comes toward the center.
steps.after: Your knight stands in front of the lone pawn, and your other knight hits it.

summary: Against the Panov, Black puts a knight on the square in front of White's lone center pawn and attacks it.
